display.title: Torah, Avodah and Gemilus Chasadim: The Three Pillars of the World
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains the three things the world stands on: learning Torah, davening to Hashem, and acts of kindness, above all tzedakah.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi teaches that, as the Sages say, the world stands on three things. Torah is our lifeline, so we set aside time to learn every day. Avodah is davening: since Hashem created and owns everything, He is the only One to turn to for whatever we need, and we pray with confidence that He listens. Gemilus chasadim means acts of kindness between people, and the outstanding one is tzedakah, which helps those who need food, clothing and shelter and also refines the giver's own character as he climbs the ladder of good deeds. Together these are the best 'diet' for a strong and healthy neshamah, and Uncle Yossi wishes everyone a summer vacation full of success for body and soul.
display.lesson: Learn Torah, daven and do kindness every day; this is Hashem's own diet for a healthy soul.

date.note: Date of episode 337, which this clip was cut from; the same talk aired in several other episodes.

sources_cited.note: Cited as 'our Chachamim tell us': the world stands on Torah, Avodah and Gemilus Chasadim.
Cited loosely as the Rambam: turn only to Hashem for whatever you need.
